+# R3 Router Replay
+
+R3 (Rollout Routing Replay) records MoE router choices during rollout and replays those
+choices during Megatron training. It is for SGLang rollout + Megatron MoE actor runs
+where rollout logprobs and training recompute logprobs can diverge because the two
+engines choose different top-k experts.
+
+The implementation uses Megatron-Core native `RouterReplay`. AReaL does not replace
+Megatron router math. It transports the routing side channel, validates it, converts it
+to Megatron token order, and drives native replay actions around each micro-batch.
+
+## Implementation
+
+End-to-end data flow:
+
+1. **Rollout recording**: `rollout.return_routed_experts=true` makes AReaL send
+   `return_routed_experts=True` to SGLang. SGLang returns base64 int32 routed expert ids
+   in `meta_info["routed_experts"]`; AReaL decodes them into
+   `[tokens, num_moe_layers * topk]`.
+1. **Workflow preprocessing**: supported workflows create two trajectory tensors:
+   `routed_experts` with shape `[batch, seq_len, num_moe_layers, topk]` and
+   `r3_routing_valid` with shape `[batch]`. Legal missing tail rows are filled from the
+   nearest previous valid row. Internal zero rows or unaligned samples are marked
+   invalid instead of being replayed.
+1. **Megatron replay**: before each Megatron micro-batch, AReaL packs routing into
+   Megatron's padded packed-token order on CPU after selecting the current PP/VPP
+   stage's MoE layers, applies CP/SP slicing on CPU, transfers only contiguous local
+   slabs, calls native `set_target_indices()`, and switches native `RouterReplayAction`
+   to `REPLAY_FORWARD`. For backward recompute it switches to `REPLAY_BACKWARD`, so
+   activation checkpointing consumes the same router choices.
+
+Key files:
+
+| File                               | Responsibility                                                                                  |
+| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `areal/engine/r3/config.py`        | Resolve MoE layer layout and router top-k from model config.                                    |
+| `areal/engine/r3/preprocess.py`    | Decode and normalize SGLang routed expert tensors.                                              |
+| `areal/engine/r3/layout.py`        | Convert workflow routing tensors to Megatron native replay slabs.                               |
+| `areal/engine/r3/discovery.py`     | Discover instance-local Megatron native `router_replay` objects.                                |
+| `areal/engine/r3/orchestration.py` | Set/clear native replay actions and target indices.                                             |
+| `areal/engine/r3/transport.py`     | Move R3 side-channel tensors through actor/engine boundaries.                                   |
+| `areal/engine/r3/asserts.py`       | Raise `R3Error` with AReaL, Megatron-Core, and mbridge versions.                                |
+| `areal/workflow/rlvr.py`           | Adds R3 tensors to RLVR trajectories when SGLang returns routing.                               |
+| `areal/trainer/ppo/actor.py`       | Feeds R3 tensors into compute-logp and PPO update; logs mismatch metrics.                       |
+| `areal/engine/megatron_engine.py`  | Initializes native replay, validates routing, drives per-micro-batch replay, and logs counters. |
+
+If a micro-batch contains invalid routing, AReaL never passes all-zero fallback rows to
+Megatron. In compute-logp (`forward_only=True`) it uses the live router. In training
+updates it records live router choices for the forward pass and replays those recorded
+choices for backward recompute, preserving forward/backward consistency.
+
+## Usage
+
+Enable R3 with the rollout-side switch:
+
+```bash
+python3 examples/math/gsm8k_rl.py --config <megatron_moe_grpo.yaml> \
+  scheduler.type=local \
+  rollout.backend=sglang:d1p1t4 \
+  actor.backend='megatron:(attn:d1p1t4|ffn:d1p1t1e4)' \
+  rollout.return_routed_experts=true \
+  actor.megatron.enable_router_replay=true \
+  actor.megatron.moe_router_fusion=false
+```
+
+Common YAML fragment:
+
+```yaml
+rollout:
+  backend: "sglang:d1p1t4"
+  return_routed_experts: true
+
+actor:
+  backend: "megatron:(attn:d1p1t4|ffn:d1p1t1e4)"
+  megatron:
+    enable_router_replay: true
+    moe_router_fusion: false
+```
+
+`rollout.return_routed_experts=true` is the main user-facing switch. In the RL trainer
+it also enables the SGLang server's internal routed-expert return flag and turns on
+`actor.megatron.enable_router_replay`. Keeping the actor flag explicit in experiment
+configs is recommended because saved configs then show the intended training path.
+
+Only the actor replays rollout routing. Reference, teacher and critic scoring use their
+own routers; their trajectory views omit the actor's routing metadata without copying
+the shared token tensors. The actor retains its original routing for logprob
+recomputation and PPO updates.
+
+For concatenated multi-turn interactions, each continuation preserves the historical
+parent routes except the parent's final sampled token. That token was not forwarded in
+the parent, so its copied placeholder is replaced by the child's captured route.
+
+Supported path:
+
+- Megatron actor backend.
+- SGLang rollout backend.
+- MoE models with discoverable router top-k and either all-MoE layers or a dense prefix
+  followed by a contiguous MoE suffix. Full-layer capture buffers may contain only
+  zero-filled dense slots before the MoE suffix.
+- Packed text RLVR and OpenAI proxy workflows.
+
+Rejected path:
+
+- vLLM rollout with `return_routed_experts=true`.
+- Non-Megatron actor backends.
+- Non-MoE actor models.
+- Sparse/interleaved MoE layouts or dense layers after the first MoE layer. These need
+  explicit global-layer metadata in rollout preprocessing and are rejected at R3
+  configuration resolution rather than silently selecting the wrong captured layers.
+- MTP layers, or `mcore-bridge` outside the experimental Qwen4Exp path below.
+- Vision workflow, tree training, or padded-sequence Megatron training.
+- Effective Megatron `moe_router_fusion=True`; native replay needs the unfused router
+  path.
+
+### Experimental Qwen Flash Next Path
+
+The Qwen4Exp / Qwen3.8 Flash Next bridge path is restricted to an all-MoE decoder,
+`WRAPPER_THD` packing and zigzag CP. Native `moe_enable_routing_replay` is passed to the
+bridge before routers are constructed. MTP, tree training, padded/model-owned packing
+and other bridge/VLM combinations remain rejected.
+
+Use the pinned Flash Next Transformers, mcore-bridge and SGLang runtime from the model
+recipe. OpenAI proxy exports must preserve processor-expanded prompt IDs, image tensors
+and token masks; the image embedding replacement must not change the captured routing
+token domain. Generic VisionRLVRWorkflow is not supported.
+
+The validated SGLang `0.5.19.dev125+g119b5ffe4` rollout image still requires the QSA
+compress-gather fix. The model patch bootstrap applies it before the selected
+SGLang/AWEX server entry point executes. The shared installer validates the source and
+transformed content against the supported SHA256 hashes. Recipes applying patches
+explicitly should use `python -m areal.engine.sglang_qsa_compress_gather`,
+`python -m areal.engine.sglang_qwen4_vl` and
+`python -m areal.engine.sglang_mm_executor`. These modules apply the guarded, idempotent
+source patches directly.
+
+Enable capture with `rollout.return_routed_experts=true`, replay with
+`actor.megatron.enable_router_replay=true`, and disable `moe_router_fusion`. The
+deployed SGLang fork's capture API must be checked separately from the legacy SGLang
+compatibility patch.
+
+This path requires a real-checkpoint GPU canary before production use: verify local
+router discovery, exact forward/recompute target IDs, CP/SP token order, queue cleanup,
+finite gradients and a successful optimizer update. Metadata checks and CPU tests alone
+do not establish full-model support.
+
+## Performance Validation
+
+R3 does not require another actor forward when `reuse_train_logp` avoids logprob
+recomputation. Capture, serialization, transport and replay still consume resources;
+there is no validated zero-overhead or fixed slowdown percentage for this
+implementation's long-context path.
+
+The current wire representation is base64 int32. With 48 MoE layers and top-k 10, a 256
+Ki-token trajectory carries approximately 480 MiB of raw routes, or 640 MiB as base64,
+excluding framing. CPU rank-local slicing reduces replay H2D volume, but does not bound
+the producer payload or RTensor request size. Binary compact routing, byte-budgeted
+transport and asynchronous capture readback require separate validation against the
+deployed SGLang version.
+
+Before claiming a performance percentage, compare matched weights, inputs, lengths,
+cache state and concurrency with capture off/on and replay off/on. Report warmup
+separately, median/p95 timings, throughput and peak host/GPU memory, alongside replay
+coverage and logprob mismatch. PP4/TP8/CP2 with full recomputation and 16K–256K contexts
+has not been validated by the small-model smoke tests.
+
+## Metrics
+
+R3 adds two groups of metrics.
+
+### Rollout/Training Logprob Mismatch
+
+These metrics are emitted under `compute_logp/r3/*` during actor recompute-logp. They
+compare SGLang rollout token logprobs with Megatron training recompute logprobs on valid
+loss tokens.
+
+These metrics are not emitted when actor recompute-logp is bypassed by
+`reuse_train_logp`; the existing loss-stage logprob mismatch metrics remain available.
+
+| Metric                                                          | Meaning                                                                                 |
+| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `compute_logp/r3/enabled`                                       | `1.0` when the batch carried R3 side-channel tensors; `0.0` otherwise.                  |
+| `compute_logp/r3/rollout_train_k3_kl/{avg,max,min}`             | Taylor KL estimate `exp(delta) - 1 - delta`, where `delta = train_logp - rollout_logp`. |
+| `compute_logp/r3/rollout_train_logp_abs_diff/{avg,max,min}`     | Absolute token logprob difference.                                                      |
+| `compute_logp/r3/rollout_train_logp_sq_diff/{avg,max,min}`      | Squared token logprob difference.                                                       |
+| `compute_logp/r3/rollout_train_extreme_frac_tau2/{avg,max,min}` | Fraction of valid tokens with `abs(delta) > log(2)`.                                    |
+| `compute_logp/r3/rollout_train_extreme_frac_tau5/{avg,max,min}` | Fraction of valid tokens with `abs(delta) > log(5)`.                                    |
+| `compute_logp/r3/n_valid_tokens`                                | Denominator for token-level mismatch statistics.                                        |
+
+### Replay Execution Counters
+
+These metrics are emitted as `r3/*` from the Megatron engine. During PPO update they can
+also appear with a trainer prefix such as `ppo_actor/update/r3/*`.
+
+| Metric                           | Meaning                                                                                       |
+| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `r3/enabled`                     | `1.0` when Megatron native router replay was used for the call.                               |
+| `r3/batches_with_side_channel`   | Batches that carried R3 tensors.                                                              |
+| `r3/samples_total`               | Number of sequences in the side channel.                                                      |
+| `r3/routing_valid_samples`       | Sequences whose rollout routing passed preprocessing validation.                              |
+| `r3/routing_invalid_samples`     | Sequences marked invalid by preprocessing.                                                    |
+| `r3/routing_valid_fraction`      | `routing_valid_samples / samples_total`.                                                      |
+| `r3/logical_microbatches`        | Megatron logical micro-batches for this call.                                                 |
+| `r3/router_stage_microbatches`   | Micro-batches on stages that contain local MoE routers.                                       |
+| `r3/replayed_microbatches`       | Micro-batches where rollout routing was replayed.                                             |
+| `r3/skipped_microbatches`        | Micro-batches where rollout routing was not safe to replay.                                   |
+| `r3/invalid_samples`             | Invalid samples that caused replay skips.                                                     |
+| `r3/mode_replay_microbatches`    | Micro-batches run in native replay mode.                                                      |
+| `r3/mode_record_microbatches`    | Training micro-batches that used native `RECORD` because rollout routing was invalid.         |
+| `r3/mode_live_microbatches`      | Forward-only micro-batches that fell back to the live router.                                 |
+| `r3/mode_no_router_microbatches` | Micro-batches on model stages without local MoE routers.                                      |
+| `r3/replay_fraction_active`      | `mode_replay_microbatches / router_stage_microbatches`; healthy R3 runs should be near `1.0`. |
+| `r3/skip_fraction_active`        | `skipped_microbatches / router_stage_microbatches`; healthy R3 runs should be near `0.0`.     |
+| `r3/tokens_real`                 | Real packed tokens seen by Megatron.                                                          |
+| `r3/tokens_padded`               | Tokens after Megatron packing/padding.                                                        |
+| `r3/tokens_padding`              | Padding tokens introduced by Megatron packing/alignment.                                      |
+| `r3/replay_real_tokens`          | Real tokens in replayed micro-batches.                                                        |
+| `r3/record_real_tokens`          | Real tokens in record-fallback micro-batches.                                                 |
+| `r3/live_real_tokens`            | Real tokens in live-router fallback micro-batches.                                            |
+| `r3/no_router_real_tokens`       | Real tokens on stages without local MoE routers.                                              |
+
+Skip reasons are sparse counters emitted only when they happen, for example
+`r3/skip_invalid_sample`, `r3/skip_zero_routing_for_real_token`, or
+`r3/skip_missing_final_token_routing_without_replacement`.
+
+## Sanity Checks
+
+For a healthy R3-on run:
+
+- `compute_logp/r3/enabled` is `1.0` on recompute-logp batches.
+- `r3/replay_fraction_active` is close to `1.0`.
+- `r3/routing_valid_fraction` is close to `1.0`.
+- `r3/skipped_microbatches` and `r3/invalid_samples` stay at `0`, or are explained by
+  rollout aborts.
+- `rollout_train_k3_kl`, `rollout_train_logp_abs_diff`, and extreme-fraction metrics are
+  materially lower than an otherwise identical R3-off run.
+
+In the GSM8K Moonlight-16B-A3B bs32/group8 validation run, both R3-on and R3-off
+completed `233/233` steps. Tail-20 mismatch metrics dropped with R3:
+
+| Metric                                |    R3 off |        R3 on |
+| ------------------------------------- | --------: | -----------: |
+| `rollout_train_k3_kl/avg`             | `0.00958` |   `0.000373` |
+| `rollout_train_logp_abs_diff/avg`     |  `0.0322` |    `0.00607` |
+| `rollout_train_extreme_frac_tau2/avg` | `0.00908` |  `0.0000681` |
+| `rollout_train_extreme_frac_tau5/avg` | `0.00133` | `0.00000397` |
+
+## Debugging
+
+`R3Error` includes package versions and shape/config context, for example:
+
+```text
+routed_experts has more token rows than the training sequence
+(areal='...', megatron-core='...', mbridge='...', raw_shape=(...), seq_len=...)
+```
+
+Typical causes:
+
+- SGLang and Megatron disagree on MoE layer count or router top-k.
+- SGLang returns routing rows that no longer match the training sequence.
+- A workflow emits `routed_experts` without the paired `r3_routing_valid` tensor.
+- `moe_router_fusion=True` bypasses the native replay-capable router path.
+
+Focused tests:
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest \
+  tests/test_r3_preprocess.py \
+  tests/test_r3_layout.py \
+  tests/test_r3_orchestration.py \
+  tests/test_r3_config_discovery.py \
+  tests/test_r3_engine_validation.py \
+  tests/test_remote_inf_engine_r3.py \
+  tests/test_ppo_actor_r3.py
+```

+    # Two sequences occupy eight padded positions each. CP rank zero owns
+    # their first and last quarters. A final dummy segment is optional.
+    full = torch.arange(16 + padding_length, dtype=torch.float32)
+    local = full[
+        torch.tensor([0, 1, 6, 7, 8, 9, 14, 15] + ([16, 19] if padding_length else []))

+    inputs = {
+        "_cp_padded_cu_seqlens": padded_cu,
+        "_cp_old_cu_seqlens": torch.tensor([0, 3, 8]),
+        "_cp_padding_length": padding_length,

+

+        assert values is local

+        return full
+

+    # sequence unpadding after the CP scalar reconstruction boundary.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(megatron_engine, "reassemble_cp_packed_logprobs", reassembled)

+        atol=0,

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from areal.api import ModelResponse
+from areal.experimental.openai.proxy.server import (
+    deserialize_interactions,
+    serialize_interactions,
+)
+from areal.experimental.openai.types import (
+    InteractionWithTokenLogpReward,
+    concat_tensor_interactions,
+)
+
+
+def _response(
+    *,
+    input_tokens: list[int],
+    output_tokens: list[int],
+    routed: np.ndarray | None,
+) -> ModelResponse:
+    return ModelResponse(
+        input_tokens=input_tokens,
+        output_tokens=output_tokens,
+        output_logprobs=[-0.1] * len(output_tokens),
+        output_versions=[1] * len(output_tokens),
+        routed_experts=routed,
+    )
+
+
+def test_interaction_to_tensor_dict_includes_r3_routing():
+    routed = np.arange(1, 1 + 3 * 4, dtype=np.int32).reshape(3, 4)
+    interaction = InteractionWithTokenLogpReward(
+        model_response=_response(
+            input_tokens=[1, 2],
+            output_tokens=[3, 4],
+            routed=routed,
+        ),
+        reward=1.0,
+        r3_num_moe_layers=2,
+        r3_topk=2,
+    )
+
+    tensor_dict = interaction.to_tensor_dict()
+
+    assert tensor_dict["routed_experts"].shape == (1, 4, 2, 2)
+    assert tensor_dict["r3_routing_valid"].tolist() == [True]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        tensor_dict["routed_experts"][0, 3],
+        tensor_dict["routed_experts"][0, 2],
+        rtol=0,
+        atol=0,
+    )
+
+
+def test_concat_interaction_to_tensor_dict_concatenates_parent_routing():
+    parent_routed = np.arange(1, 1 + 2 * 4, dtype=np.int32).reshape(2, 4)
+    child_routed = np.arange(101, 101 + 5 * 4, dtype=np.int32).reshape(5, 4)
+    parent = InteractionWithTokenLogpReward(
+        model_response=_response(
+            input_tokens=[1],
+            output_tokens=[2, 3],
+            routed=parent_routed,
+        ),
+        chat_template_type="concat",
+        r3_num_moe_layers=2,
+        r3_topk=2,
+    )
+    child = InteractionWithTokenLogpReward(
+        model_response=_response(
+            input_tokens=[1, 2, 3, 4],
+            output_tokens=[5, 6],
+            routed=child_routed,
+        ),
+        parent=parent,
+        chat_template_type="concat",
+        r3_num_moe_layers=2,
+        r3_topk=2,
+    )
+
+    tensor_dict = child.to_tensor_dict()
+
+    routed = tensor_dict["routed_experts"]
+    assert routed.shape == (1, 6, 2, 2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        routed[0, :2],
+        parent.to_tensor_dict()["routed_experts"][0, :2],
+        rtol=0,
+        atol=0,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        routed[0, 2:],
+        torch.as_tensor(
+            np.stack(
+                [
+                    child_routed.reshape(5, 2, 2)[2],
+                    child_routed.reshape(5, 2, 2)[3],
+                    child_routed.reshape(5, 2, 2)[4],

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("invalid_turn", [None, 0, 1, 2])
+def test_concat_three_turns_preserves_historical_routes_and_validity(invalid_turn):
+    """Each continuation replaces only its parent's unforwarded final row."""
+    parent = None
+    expected = None
+    cached = []
+    for turn in range(3):
+        input_tokens = list(range(1, 2 * turn + 2))
+        output_tokens = [2 * turn + 2]
+        seq_len = len(input_tokens) + 1
+        raw = np.arange(1, 1 + (seq_len - 1) * 4, dtype=np.int32).reshape(-1, 4)
+        raw += 100 * turn
+        if turn == invalid_turn:
+            raw[:] = 0
+        interaction = InteractionWithTokenLogpReward(
+            model_response=_response(
+                input_tokens=input_tokens, output_tokens=output_tokens, routed=raw
+            ),
+            parent=parent,
+            chat_template_type="concat",
+            r3_num_moe_layers=2,
+            r3_topk=2,
+        )
+        result = interaction.to_tensor_dict()
+        if invalid_turn is None:
+            current = torch.as_tensor(raw).reshape(-1, 2, 2)
+            current = torch.cat([current, current[-1:]])
+            expected = (
+                current
+                if expected is None
+                else torch.cat([expected[:-1], current[expected.shape[0] - 1 :]])
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                result["routed_experts"][0], expected, rtol=0, atol=0
+            )
+        assert result["r3_routing_valid"].item() == (
+            invalid_turn is None or turn < invalid_turn
+        )
+        cached.append(result["routed_experts"].clone())
+        parent = interaction
+    # Exporting a child must not mutate cached parent routing.
+    ancestor = parent
+    for snapshot in reversed(cached):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            ancestor.to_tensor_dict()["routed_experts"], snapshot, rtol=0, atol=0
+        )
+        ancestor = ancestor.parent

+class _FakeR3Engine:
+    def __init__(self, forward_result=None, *, r3_enabled=True, require_r3=True):
+        self._r3_enabled = r3_enabled
+        self._r3_pending_routed_experts = None
+        self._r3_pending_valid = None
+        self.forward_result = forward_result
+        self.require_r3 = require_r3
+
+    def eval(self):
+        self.eval_called = True
+
+    def forward(self, input_, aggregate_fn):
+        assert "routed_experts" not in input_
+        assert "r3_routing_valid" not in input_
+        if self.require_r3:
+            assert self._r3_pending_routed_experts is not None
+            assert self._r3_pending_valid is not None
+        if self.forward_result is not None:
+            return self.forward_result
+        return aggregate_fn([torch.ones(1), torch.ones(1)])
+
+

+        "r3_routing_valid": valid,
+    }

+    assert engine._r3_pending_routed_experts is None
+    assert engine._r3_pending_valid is None
+    assert data["routed_experts"] is routed
+    assert data["r3_routing_valid"] is valid

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from areal.engine.r3.asserts import R3Error
+from areal.engine.r3.config import resolve_moe_layer_indices, resolve_r3_moe_config

+def test_resolve_r3_moe_config_handles_dense_prefix_and_freq_list():
+    cfg = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_layers=6,
+        moe_layer_freq=[1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1],
+        first_k_dense_replace=2,
+        moe_router_topk=4,
+    )
+
+    resolved = resolve_r3_moe_config(cfg)
+
+    assert resolved.num_moe_layers == 2
+    assert resolved.moe_layer_indices == (4, 5)
+    assert resolved.global_to_moe_index == {4: 0, 5: 1}
+    assert resolved.topk == 4
+
+
+def test_resolve_r3_moe_config_accepts_omegaconf_list_config():
+    from omegaconf import OmegaConf
+
+    cfg = OmegaConf.create(
+        {
+            "num_layers": 4,
+            "moe_layer_freq": [0, 0, 1, 1],
+            "moe_router_topk": 2,
+        }
+    )
+
+    resolved = resolve_r3_moe_config(cfg)
+
+    assert resolved.moe_layer_indices == (2, 3)
+    assert resolved.num_moe_layers == 2
+
+
+def test_resolve_r3_moe_config_accepts_hf_num_hidden_layers():
+    cfg = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_hidden_layers=4,
+        first_k_dense_replace=1,
+        num_experts_per_tok=2,
+    )
+
+    resolved = resolve_r3_moe_config(cfg)
+
+    assert resolved.num_layers == 4
+    assert resolved.moe_layer_indices == (1, 2, 3)
+    assert resolved.num_moe_layers == 3
+    assert resolved.topk == 2
+
+
+def test_resolve_r3_moe_config_rejects_flat_dim_guessing():
+    cfg = SimpleNamespace(num_layers=2, moe_layer_freq=1)
+
+    with pytest.raises(R3Error, match="Unable to resolve MoE router topk"):
+        resolve_r3_moe_config(cfg)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("freq", "dense_prefix", "expected"),
+    [
+        (1, 0, (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)),
+        (2, 0, (0, 2, 4)),
+        (3, 0, (0, 3)),
+        (2, 2, (2, 4)),
+        (9, 0, (0,)),
+    ],
+)
+def test_integer_moe_frequency_matches_native_mcore(freq, dense_prefix, expected):
+    """MCore counts periodic MoE layers from zero, including dense prefixes."""
+    config = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_layers=6,
+        moe_router_topk=2,
+        moe_layer_freq=freq,
+        first_k_dense_replace=dense_prefix,
+    )
+    assert resolve_moe_layer_indices(config) == expected
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("freq", [0, -2])
+def test_integer_moe_frequency_rejects_nonpositive_values(freq):
+    """Do not invent a decoder layout for unsupported periodic frequencies."""
+    with pytest.raises(R3Error, match="moe_layer_freq must be positive"):
+        resolve_r3_moe_config(
+            SimpleNamespace(num_layers=4, moe_router_topk=2, moe_layer_freq=freq)
+        )

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_getter", [False, True])

+        num_hidden_layers=6,
+        num_experts_per_tok=3,

+def test_discover_native_router_replay_collects_instance_refs(monkeypatch):
+    class FakeRouter(torch.nn.Module):
+        def __init__(self, replay):
+            super().__init__()
+            self.router_replay = replay
+
+    class FakeLayer(torch.nn.Module):
+        def __init__(self):
+            super().__init__()
+            self.router = FakeRouter(replay=object())
+
+    model = torch.nn.Module()
+    model.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList([FakeLayer(), FakeLayer()])
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        "areal.engine.r3.discovery._resolve_topk_router_type",
+        lambda: FakeRouter,
+    )
+
+    grouped = discover_native_router_replay(model)
+
+    refs = grouped[0]
+    assert len(refs) == 2
+    assert [ref.layer_number for ref in refs] == [0, 1]
+    assert [ref.layer_number_is_global for ref in refs] == [False, False]
+    assert refs[0].router_replay is model.layers[0].router.router_replay
+    assert refs[1].router_replay is model.layers[1].router.router_replay
+

+    class FakeRouter(torch.nn.Module):
+        def __init__(self, layer_number: int):
+            super().__init__()
+            self.router_replay = object()
+            self.layer_number = layer_number
+
+    model = torch.nn.Module()
+    model.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList([FakeRouter(3)])
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        "areal.engine.r3.discovery._resolve_topk_router_type",
+        lambda: FakeRouter,
+    )
+
+    refs = discover_native_router_replay(model)[0]
+
+    assert refs[0].layer_number == 2
+    assert refs[0].layer_number_is_global

+        router_replay = None
+

+    token_logprobs: list[tuple[float, int]],

+    *,
+    routed_experts: np.ndarray | None = None,
+    prompt_tokens: int | None = None,
+    completion_tokens: int | None = None,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    meta_info: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "finish_reason": {
+            "type": finish_reason_type,
+            "message": "",
+        },
+        "output_token_logprobs": token_logprobs,
+    }
+    if routed_experts is not None:
+        if prompt_tokens is None or completion_tokens is None:
+            raise ValueError("prompt_tokens and completion_tokens are required")
+        meta_info["prompt_tokens"] = prompt_tokens
+        meta_info["completion_tokens"] = completion_tokens
+        meta_info["routed_experts"] = base64.b64encode(
+            np.asarray(routed_experts, dtype=np.int32).tobytes()
+        ).decode("utf-8")
+    return {"meta_info": meta_info}
+
+
+def _make_engine(*, return_routed_experts: bool = True) -> RemoteInfEngine:
+    engine = RemoteInfEngine(
+        InferenceEngineConfig(
+            backend="sglang:d1",
+            return_routed_experts=return_routed_experts,
+        ),

+    )

+    engine._workflow_executor = SimpleNamespace(is_paused=lambda: False)

+    first_routing = np.arange(1, 1 + 4 * 4, dtype=np.int32).reshape(4, 4)
+    second_routing = np.concatenate(
+        [
+            first_routing,

+        ],

+    )

+                routed_experts=first_routing,
+                prompt_tokens=3,

`_pack_routing_to_padded_order()` re-validates for all-zero rows and uses multiple `.item()` calls (`torch.any(...).item()`, `zero_rows[-1].item()`), which will synchronize CPU<->GPU if `routed_experts` is on GPU during training. Consider relying on `routing_valid` and removing the clone/zero-row checks here (or moving this validation to the CPU-side preprocessing step).

+            num_sgl_tokens=num_sgl_tokens,
+        )
+    return flat.reshape(num_sgl_tokens, -1)
+
+
+def _reshape_routed_experts(
+    routed_experts: np.ndarray,
+    *,
+    num_moe_layers: int,
+    topk: int,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    arr = np.asarray(routed_experts, dtype=np.int32)
+    if arr.ndim == 2:
+        expected_flat_dim = num_moe_layers * topk
+        if arr.shape[1] % topk != 0:
+            raise r3_error(
+                "routed_experts flat_dim does not match Megatron MoE config",
+                raw_shape=arr.shape,
+                flat_dim=arr.shape[1],
+                num_moe_layers=num_moe_layers,
+                topk=topk,
+                expected_flat_dim=expected_flat_dim,
+            )
+        returned_layers = arr.shape[1] // topk
+        if returned_layers < num_moe_layers:
+            raise r3_error(
+                "routed_experts flat_dim does not match Megatron MoE config",
+                raw_shape=arr.shape,
+                flat_dim=arr.shape[1],
+                num_moe_layers=num_moe_layers,
+                topk=topk,
+                expected_flat_dim=expected_flat_dim,
+                returned_layers=returned_layers,
+            )
+        arr = arr.reshape(arr.shape[0], returned_layers, topk)
+        if returned_layers > num_moe_layers:
+            arr = arr[:, returned_layers - num_moe_layers :, :]
+        return arr
+    if arr.ndim == 3:
+        if arr.shape[2] == topk and arr.shape[1] > num_moe_layers:
+            return arr[:, arr.shape[1] - num_moe_layers :, :]
+        if arr.shape[1:] != (num_moe_layers, topk):
+            raise r3_error(
+                "routed_experts layer/topk dims do not match Megatron MoE config",
+                raw_shape=arr.shape,
+                num_moe_layers=num_moe_layers,
+                topk=topk,
+            )
+        return arr
+    raise r3_error("Unsupported routed_experts ndim", raw_shape=arr.shape)
+
+
+def _nearest_valid_row(rows: np.ndarray, before: int) -> np.ndarray | None:
+    for idx in range(before - 1, -1, -1):
+        row = rows[idx]
+        if not np.all(row == 0):
+            return row
+    return None
+
+
+def _preprocess_one(
+    routed_experts: np.ndarray | None,
+    *,
+    seq_len: int,
+    num_moe_layers: int,
+    topk: int,
+) -> tuple[np.ndarray, bool]:
+    out = np.zeros((seq_len, num_moe_layers, topk), dtype=np.int32)
+    if routed_experts is None:
+        return out, False
+
+    arr = _reshape_routed_experts(
+        routed_experts,
+        num_moe_layers=num_moe_layers,
+        topk=topk,
+    )
+    if arr.shape[0] > seq_len:
+        raise r3_error(
+            "routed_experts has more token rows than the training sequence",
+            raw_shape=arr.shape,
+            seq_len=seq_len,
+        )
+
+    copied = arr.shape[0]
+    if copied > 0:
+        out[:copied] = arr
+
+    valid = copied >= max(seq_len - 1, 0)
+    for pos in range(copied, seq_len):
+        replacement = _nearest_valid_row(out, pos)
+        if replacement is not None:
+            out[pos] = replacement
+
+    real_rows_to_check = max(seq_len - 1, 0)
+    if real_rows_to_check > 0:
+        zero_rows = np.all(out[:real_rows_to_check] == 0, axis=(1, 2))
+        if bool(np.any(zero_rows)):
+            valid = False
+            for pos in np.nonzero(zero_rows)[0]:
+                replacement = _nearest_valid_row(out, int(pos))
+                if replacement is not None:
+                    out[pos] = replacement
+
+    if seq_len > 0 and np.all(out[-1] == 0):
+        replacement = _nearest_valid_row(out, seq_len - 1)
+        if replacement is not None:
+            out[-1] = replacement
+

Reviewed R3 head `8f3e0d3904376496974b8c0f014d0dd11870dd76` against the Qwen3.8 Flash Next integration in #1774. The documented supported path does not yet cover that model/bridge combination. I found these issues in the implementation:

1. **[P1] Multi-turn concat keeps the fabricated route for the parent's final token.** [types.py:231–237](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/8f3e0d3904376496974b8c0f014d0dd11870dd76/areal/experimental/openai/types.py#L231-L237) appends the complete parent routing to `current_routed[parent_len:]`. The parent final sampled token was never forwarded, so preprocessing fills its missing route by copying an earlier token. In the child prompt this token is actually forwarded and has a real captured route, but that row is discarded. For parent `[1,2,3]` and child `[1,2,3,4,5,6]`, position 2 retains the copied route rather than the child's real route. This affects subsequent attention/recurrent state. The join should be `parent[:-1] + current[parent_len-1:]`; the existing concat test currently asserts the incorrect seam behavior.

2. **[P1] R3 with a reference model fails at reference scoring.** [actor.py:304–307](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/8f3e0d3904376496974b8c0f014d0dd11870dd76/areal/trainer/ppo/actor.py#L304-L307) rejects routing metadata when the engine has replay disabled. RLTrainer passes the original R3 rollout batch to `ref.compute_logp`, while automatically enabling replay only for the actor. A normal reference-KL configuration therefore raises on its first scoring call. Reference scoring should receive a copy without `routed_experts` / `r3_routing_valid`, preserving the actor's original batch. Replaying the actor's choices in the reference model would change reference semantics. The current #1774 recipe uses zero KL and does not trigger this issue.

3. **[P2] Integer MoE frequency uses a different layer origin from native MCore.** [config.py:40–41](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/8f3e0d3904376496974b8c0f014d0dd11870dd76/areal/engine/r3/config.py#L40-L41) starts at `freq - 1`, whereas [MCore 0.19's decoder construction](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/core_v0.19.0/megatron/core/models/gpt/gpt_layer_specs.py#L615-L618) selects `i % freq == 0`. With `freq=2`, discovery expects layers 1,3 while native routers are on 0,2. Please derive the actual router layout or account for backend conventions explicitly. Qwen's all-MoE layout does not trigger this case.

4. **[P2] Routing unpadding uses the top-k axis instead of the sequence axis.** [data.py:327–335](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/8f3e0d3904376496974b8c0f014d0dd11870dd76/areal/utils/data.py#L327-L335) trims the last dimension for all tensors. Newly transported routing is `[N,S,L,K]`, so ordinary short trajectories retain full batch-length routing padding; a valid sequence shorter than K has its top-k dimension truncated. Routing needs sequence-aware trimming on dimension 1.

For running **Qwen3.8 Flash Next on #1774**, additional adaptation is required:

- HF-side R3 configuration must unwrap `get_text_config()` / `text_config`. Both proxy configuration and RLTrainer currently resolve the outer Qwen4Exp config, which has no top-level MoE top-k/layer attributes, and fail with `Unable to resolve MoE router topk`.
- The explicit `mcore-bridge` and vision guards need a narrowly supported Qwen4Exp packed path. The bridge must also receive `moe_enable_routing_replay=True` before routers are constructed; removing the guards alone is insufficient.
- #1774 uses AWEX with rollout v1. This launcher bypasses the new v2 capture compatibility hooks. Their applicability needs checking against the deployed SGLang version; this is an integration gap, not evidence that every fork will fail capture.
- At 48 layers × top-k 10 × int32, a 256Ki-token trajectory carries **480 MiB raw routing** (about 640 MiB as base64). Twelve such trajectories carry **5.625 GiB raw**, before copies/padding. RTensor fetching batches by shard count and reads whole JSON responses, so byte-budgeted transport and prefix-copy lifetime need validation for long contexts.
- Actual PP4/TP8/CP2 with full activation recomputation needs a canary. The current CPU layout/FIFO tests do not establish correctness for that topology. With `reuse_train_logp`, the new `compute_logp/r3/*` metrics are also bypassed; existing loss-stage logp mismatch metrics remain available.

This is a static source/config review with expert consultation. No GPU experiment was launched for this review.

Performance follow-up on R3 head `8f3e0d3904376496974b8c0f014d0dd11870dd76`, focusing on the long-context Qwen3.8 Flash Next workload in #1774.

**There is no validated R3-on/off wall-time comparison for this workload yet, so I cannot substantiate a “5%/10% slowdown” or “zero overhead” claim.** The Qwen bridge/vision guards identified above also prevent a direct benchmark of this PR as-is. With the target recipe's `recompute_logprob=false` and `reuse_train_logp`, R3 does not force an additional actor logprob forward; overhead instead comes from capture/readback, serialization/transport, layout preparation and replay kernels. The [R3 paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11370v1) describes no added computational overhead, but that does not measure this implementation's long-context data movement.

The route payload alone can be calculated exactly: `tokens × 48 layers × topk 10 × 4 bytes` for int32. Excluding framing and the one-row alignment difference:

| Sequence length | Raw int32 | Base64 int32 | Proposed binary int16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 Ki tokens | 30 MiB | 40 MiB | 15 MiB |
| 32 Ki tokens | 60 MiB | 80 MiB | 30 MiB |
| 128 Ki tokens | 240 MiB | 320 MiB | 120 MiB |
| 256 Ki tokens | 480 MiB | 640 MiB | 240 MiB |

These are byte costs, **not measured latency or throughput losses**. Twelve maximum-length trajectories already contain 5.625 GiB of raw int32 routes before padding/copies.

I would prioritize these optimizations:

1. **Prepare only the rank's required routes before H2D, and avoid GPU-to-Python metadata synchronization.** [engine.py:1814–1819](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/8f3e0d3904376496974b8c0f014d0dd11870dd76/areal/engine/megatron_engine.py#L1814-L1819) transfers the complete `[B,S,48,10]` tensor to every rank, then [layout.py:184–196](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/8f3e0d3904376496974b8c0f014d0dd11870dd76/areal/engine/r3/layout.py#L184-L196) packs, CP/SP-slices and finally selects local PP layers. For balanced PP4/CP2/TP8+SP, local int32 route elements are 1/64 of the full tensor, before the int64 index conversion; this is a theoretical data-volume reduction, not a 64× speedup. Build the routing layout from the original CPU microbatch metadata, select local layers/tokens, and transfer contiguous pinned slabs once. Currently cu-seqlens are moved to GPU and converted back with `.tolist()` in the layout hot path. Retain exactly the same padding, CP zigzag order and SP ordering.

2. **Overlap capture readback, with explicit buffer/event ownership.** The [upstream SGLang v0.5.10 capture path](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/v0.5.10/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/routed_experts_capturer.py#L202-L206) performs synchronous `.cpu()` readback after forwards and explicitly notes broken scheduler overlap. Current [upstream `TopkCaptureOutput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a65b776963d3e9139a82ac38fced030d0bbb6acf/python/sglang/srt/state_capturer/base.py#L100-L118) and [deferred readback](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a65b776963d3e9139a82ac38fced030d0bbb6acf/python/sglang/srt/state_capturer/base.py#L192-L220) provide a concrete reference for result-copy stream/event handling. Check the deployed fork first; port the compatible path rather than assuming the newest API exists. The piecewise-graph compatibility guard can itself affect prefill, but should only be relaxed after capture correctness is proven. #1774's AWEX v1 launcher also needs this version-aware check.

3. **Use lossless compact storage/transport and bound requests by bytes.** Qwen's expert IDs 0–511 fit int16; uint8 values would corrupt them. This halves raw storage, and binary int16 is 62.5% smaller than base64 int32. Preserve dtype/shape/version metadata and validate ranges before narrowing; convert to the native replay index dtype at consumption. [veRL's recorded-route transport](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/1d367a4f459a43768f76312c0d3430a99ec46b8c/verl/utils/megatron/router_replay_utils.py#L321-L327) uses int16 with byte views, including a [NCCL byte-view path](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/1d367a4f459a43768f76312c0d3430a99ec46b8c/verl/utils/megatron/router_replay_utils.py#L718-L721); this is a representation reference, not evidence that its entire R3 path has zero overhead. Here RTensor batches by shard count and reads complete JSON bodies. Add byte-budgeted chunks/binary payloads, sequence-aware unpadding and prompt release of rejected-group route storage.

4. **Return and retain incremental routes for multi-turn continuations.** [slime's `routed_experts_start_len`](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/58b0878679de339ec7844b45d884a87955a134be/slime/rollout/sglang_rollout.py#L190-L199) avoids retransmitting already captured rows, and its [chunk append](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/58b0878679de339ec7844b45d884a87955a134be/slime/utils/types.py#L498-L507) avoids repeatedly concatenating growing prefixes. Its [bounded microbatch prefetcher](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/58b0878679de339ec7844b45d884a87955a134be/slime/utils/routed_experts.py#L137-L155) is another useful reference. Preserve token identity, policy-version boundaries and the final-token seam; never substitute a later policy's routes for historical routes. Prompt tokens still need replay because they affect attention/recurrent state.

5. **Keep replay targets through their matching recompute-backward and profile the native kernels.** Avoid refetching/repacking a microbatch for every layer or recomputation, and bound retained FIFO/prefetch storage to in-flight microbatches. [Native MCore replay](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/core_v0.19.0/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router_replay.py#L168-L179) already reuses queued IDs during recomputation and replaces top-k with a gather of current scores. Keep that behavior, score normalization and gradient flow. Validate IDs once at ingestion and avoid repeated full-batch range scans/minibatch copies of immutable route data. Measure the actual fused/unfused routing path before proposing a kernel change.

Before quoting an overhead percentage, please publish a matched-input comparison: (A) capture off/replay off; (B) capture on/replay off to isolate producer/transport costs; (C) identical captured batches with replay off/on to isolate consumer costs; (D) end-to-end R3 off/on. Use the same weights, token sequences/lengths, concurrency, cache state, PP4/TP8/CP2 and full recomputation. Cover 16K/32K/128K/256K plus representative multi-turn trajectories; separate warmup and report median/p95 across repetitions. Record prefill/decode throughput, TTFT/ITL, capture D2H time, serialization/RPC/H2D/layout time, peak host/GPU memory, train tokens/s, accepted groups/hour and completed updates/hour. Report both `(T_on/T_off - 1)` latency increase and `(1 - throughput_on/throughput_off)` throughput loss, alongside replay coverage and logp mismatch so a faster but incomplete replay is not accepted.

Validate layout and recompute gradients against a recorded-training-route control. This follow-up is source-based analysis; no new GPU performance benchmark was run.

## Flash Next closed-loop validation

Validated commit `303ec290c26829a09e529e7ea7d60404558236c8` on the full `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` checkpoint: **three consecutive fresh rollout → PPO update → weight exchange cycles passed**, followed by generation using weight version 3. Slurm job `977093` used four 8-GPU nodes (32 GPUs) in reservation `zjw-fp8`.

- Actor topology: TP4 / PP4 / CP2 / EP8 / ETP1; packed `WRAPPER_THD`, zigzag CP, native R3 replay, router fusion and MTP disabled. Actor image: `areal-dev-sglang-0821.sif` (Megatron Core 0.17).
- Each cycle generated eight **fresh** 16K trajectories (four text, four image): 16,368 prompt tokens + 16 generated tokens; all eight training microbatches were real, with no dummy rows. Full 48-layer / 512-expert / top-10 routing was captured and replayed.
- The actor used full CPU Adam offload with existing Megatron runtime settings and warmup disabled, so all three cycles performed nonzero updates. The same Megatron PPO actor and optimizer persisted across all cycles. Adam counters advanced 1 → 2 → 3; sampled moment hashes were preserved across offload/onload; gradients were finite and parameters changed after each successful optimizer update.
- Every rank compared native forward and checkpoint-recompute replay against an independent CP/SP layout reference, checked FIFO consumption, and verified replay queues were cleared between phases and cycles.
- Each actor update exported HF weights and installed them into the same persistent SGLang service via `update_weights_from_disk`. The server reported versions 1 → 2 → 3. A BF16 embedding slice that **changed from the previous version** was read back from the live inference worker and matched the corresponding exported checkpoint exactly after each exchange.
- Rollout ran SGLang `0.5.19.dev125+g119b5ffe4` in `deepep-base-119b5ffe.sif` with TP4 / EP4 and PLE CPU offload. Actor and rollout took turns using GPU memory. Maximum actor PyTorch allocated memory was 70.39 GiB per rank (this excludes non-PyTorch/server allocations).

| Step | Global gradient norm | Learning rate | Adam step | Installed SGLang version | Live weight probe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0.02894265018 | 3e-06 | 1 | 1 | changed and matched |
| 2 | 0.008443719707 | 3e-06 | 2 | 2 | changed and matched |
| 3 | 0.03659226373 | 3e-06 | 3 | 3 | changed and matched |

Scope: this is a controlled PPO/R3 integration canary driven through `MegatronPPOActor` and native SGLang APIs, with alternating rewards and one optimizer minibatch per cycle; it does not establish task quality or reward convergence. Weight exchange was **HF disk transport**, so AWEX zero-copy exchange, Arena task execution, recovery, and long-running stability are not covered. Rollout uses the separate compatible SGLang image listed above; only the actor uses the requested 0821 image.

The branch merged main at `aedc21ec66ff03f329dcd4139945da8087e0d0e7` and PR #1774 at `a1afb2461565f719ef090e4cd28fbf197bbf809b` for the Flash Next runtime fixes. #1774 is a dependency; R3-specific additions narrowly enable the supported Qwen4Exp packed path and repair CP reassembly for chunked forward logprobs.

Local regression: focused R3, PPO, Flash Next, transport, and SGLang-patch tests **559 passed / 10 skipped**. Skips were one CUDA test in the CPU run, eight tests requiring an explicit local Qwen model environment variable, and one Core 0.19-only compatibility test against the Core 0.17 actor image. `pre-commit run --all-files` passed. GPU closed-loop reports cover all 32 actor ranks.

Reproduction artifacts on the cluster: `/storage/openpsi/users/wanghaitao.wht/areal_runs/r3-flash-next-20261012/closed-loop-3steps/run-977093` (immutable actor/driver/server scripts, per-step rollout and exchange manifests, 32 rank reports, driver report, and logs). CPU/pre-commit logs are in `/storage/openpsi/users/wanghaitao.wht/areal_runs/r3-flash-next-20261012/closed-loop-3steps`.

CI was triggered for this head by removing and re-adding `safe-to-test`. Both SGLang and vLLM unit-test variants **passed** ([workflow run](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/actions/runs/38237686505)); remote pre-commit and package-installation checks also passed.

@yulangz Thanks for the three-cycle Flash Next closed-loop validation on `303ec290c26829a09e529e7ea7d60404558236c8`. It is useful evidence for the packed, all-MoE Qwen path. I reviewed this head against the Arena/AWEX rollout path and found two follow-ups:

1. **Sparse-MoE layer mapping can silently replay the wrong layers.** [`_reshape_routed_experts`](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/303ec290c26829a09e529e7ea7d60404558236c8/areal/engine/r3/preprocess.py#L66-L109) takes the last `num_moe_layers` slots when SGLang returns more layers. SGLang's capturer indexes its full `num_hidden_layers` buffer by global `layer_id`, so interleaved dense layers are not necessarily a leading prefix. For example, with MoE layers 0, 2, and 4 of six, this code selects slots 3, 4, and 5. The current validity check can miss this because other layers in the token row are nonzero. Please select the configured `moe_layer_indices` for a full-layer payload, or reject sparse MoE explicitly until that layout is supported. This does not affect the validated all-MoE Qwen configuration.

2. **A missing-route leaf can fail an entire grouped export instead of taking the invalid-routing fallback.** [`_r3_tensor_dict`](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/303ec290c26829a09e529e7ea7d60404558236c8/areal/experimental/openai/types.py#L325-L339) omits both R3 keys when a response has no routes, while a sibling leaf with routes includes them. [`concat_tensor_interactions`](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/303ec290c26829a09e529e7ea7d60404558236c8/areal/experimental/openai/types.py#L380-L399) then reaches the exact-key check in `concat_padded_tensors` and raises. The remote inference missing-route guard allows the empty-output case because it checks `accumulated_output_tokens`. If such a response is exported as a usable leaf, please emit zero-filled routes with `r3_routing_valid=False` and add a mixed valid/missing-route group test.

The existing Arena launch recipe I checked is still pinned to an earlier checkout and has `return_routed_experts: false`; it also invokes the example QSA patch module removed in this PR. It needs a small launch/config migration before it can exercise this head. The three-cycle canary validates the core Qwen path, while the target Arena/AWEX run remains a separate end-to-end check.

@yulangz Follow-up/correction to [my review comment](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/pull/1496#issuecomment-6139419159): our current rollout image uses **SGLang 0.5.19**, and the QSA compress-gather fix is still required for the Flash Next run. Please **keep this fix active** during the launch/config migration; removing the old YAML command alone is not sufficient evidence that the running server is patched.

I see that this PR moves the same source-hash-validated fix to [`areal.engine.sglang_qsa_compress_gather`](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/303ec290c26829a09e529e7ea7d60404558236c8/areal/engine/sglang_qsa_compress_gather.py) and intends to apply it through [`sglang_model_patches`](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/blob/303ec290c26829a09e529e7ea7d60404558236c8/areal/engine/sglang_model_patches.py) before server startup. The existing recipe still invokes the deleted `examples.swe.qwen38_flash_next.patch_sglang_qsa_compress_gather` module. Could we retain a compatibility entrypoint for that command (or update the recipe to invoke the new module explicitly) until the automatic AWEX/SGLang startup path has been verified on the actual 0.5.19 image? A startup check of the installed `qsa_indexer.py` against `PATCHED_SHA256` would make the requirement unambiguous. The goal is to preserve the QSA fix, not to remove it as part of adopting R3.

Rebased and squashed the branch onto latest main; current commit `a8b33762`.

Current branch: `a8b3376261d72dc769950eab7a10fe7958e46eeb`, rebased and squashed onto main `ba237a1b` (including final #1774 and #1782).

- Removed the old #1774 snapshot's withdrawn Graybox instruction preprocessor and diagnostic-replay RPC special case. Other Flash Next recipe files match main; the three additional legacy patch CLI modules are intentional 7-line delegates to the canonical engine patch modules.
- Preserve SGLang 0.5.19's required QSA fix and verify the installed `qsa_indexer.py` SHA before server exec; retain old patch commands for existing launch recipes. Earlier actual-image CPU verification was Slurm job `977811` on `deepep-base-119b5ffe.sif` (`0.5.19.dev125+g119b5ffe4`), validating installed SHA `72c5d471a67729446ec9b1c0d810bc87bc85149c381c213adfb4119eddde9a7c`. This was a bootstrap check before exec, not a new inference/AWEX run.
- Address review comments by rejecting unsupported sparse/interleaved MoE layouts and emitting invalid zero routes for missing-route grouped leaves, including late-configured cached leaves.
- Local regression in `areal-dev-sglang-0821.sif`: **1543 passed / 21 skipped**, including new main named-loss tests and existing R3/PPO/Flash Next/transport/Arena tests. Skips require CUDA, external mcore-bridge, Transformers 5.16.1 references, a local Qwen model, or Core 0.19. Full `pre-commit run --all-files` and Conventional Commit checks passed.
- CI is retriggered using `safe-to-test` for this new head; no result is claimed yet. No fresh multi-node run was performed for this rebase. The three-cycle GPU canary below remains evidence for historical commit `303ec290`, and did not initialize W&B or persist numerical actor/rollout logp differences.

Local logs and scripts: `/storage/openpsi/users/wanghaitao.wht/areal_runs/r3-main-rebase-20261014`.

Fixed CI runner provisioning in `949d3d73`. [The preceding run](https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL/actions/runs/38555348058) failed before either unit-test variant started: both runner registration tokens were created at approximately 11:16 UTC, but GPU capacity retries delayed VM creation until 12:30 UTC. The tokens were already older than their [one-hour validity](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#create-a-registration-token-for-a-repository). VM startup logs were unavailable after cleanup, so no direct VM-side registration error is claimed.

The workflow now fetches a fresh registration token before each zone allocation attempt and stops on token API errors, preserving the existing cleanup. This prevents accumulated cross-zone resource waits from exhausting a token's lifetime; it does not change R3, SGLang, or AReaL launchers.

Validation: **3 regression tests passed**, exercising zone retry/token rotation and failures of the first or second token request; all workflow shell steps passed `bash -n`; full `pre-commit run --all-files` and Conventional Commit checks passed. No GPU integration run was needed for this workflow-only fix. Logs/scripts: `/storage/openpsi/users/wanghaitao.wht/areal_runs/r3-ci-fix-20261014`.

CI has been retriggered using `safe-to-test` for this head; no new CI result is claimed. The R3 rebase regression and GPU canary remain tied to their documented earlier commits.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces R3 (Rollout Routing Replay) to record MoE router choices during SGLang rollout and replay them during Megatron training, preventing logprob divergence. It adds a new `areal/engine/r3` module, integrates replay logic into the Megatron engine, updates the PPO actor and RL trainer, and includes SGLang compatibility patches. The review feedback highlights several critical issues: performance bottlenecks in `layout.py` caused by synchronous GPU-to-CPU transfers inside a loop, a compatibility issue with OmegaConf `ListConfig` types in `config.py`, a wrap-around bug in the PPO actor's drift metrics calculation, and a signature mismatch in a data proxy test.

## Pull request overview This PR adds end-to-end R3 (Rollout Routing Replay) support to make SGLang MoE rollout routing reproducible during Megatron MoE actor training by transporting routed-expert tensors, validating/packing them into Megatron token order, and driving Megatron-Core native `RouterReplay` during recompute-logp and PPO updates. **Changes:** - Introduces a new `areal/engine/r3` module (config discovery, preprocessing/validation, packing/layout, orchestration, side-channel transport) and wires it into Megatron engine execution. - Extends rollout/workflow/proxy/v2 inference-service paths to request, decode, preserve, and export `routed_experts`, plus adds rollout/train mismatch + replay health metrics. - Adds docs and examples for R3 usage, plus test coverage across preprocessing, layout, orchestration, proxy serialization, and remote inference retry stitching. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 60 out of 62 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.
